title: System by Dave runtime context, envelope and storage contract
description: Three separate contracts in one file: $defs/context says what the shared context means; $defs/envelope says how it moves; $defs/storageRecord says where it rests. Products adopt them independently. The top level validates a context object. See docs/client-framework.md.

context.description: SBDContext. client is always injected from the build of the serving surface; a product must ignore any client value that arrives from a URL, envelope or storage record.

returnTo.description: Absolute https URL of the parent destination. Must be on a surface listed in the active client manifest; anything else is dropped (no open redirects).

session.description: Show context. Mirrors the existing sbd* URL parameters (sbdShow, sbdVenue, sbdDate, sbdOperator, sbdPhase) so today's links keep working.

operator.description: Sensitive: a person's name. Allowed in same-origin storage; never in a cross-origin envelope.

envelope.description: How context and a handoff move. Transport priority: same origin -> storage record; cross origin -> URL fragment #sbd=<base64url(JSON)>; larger or sensitive payloads -> transfer.html or a file handoff. The fragment form is bounded: encoded length <= 2048 bytes, no operator field, no payload containing personal data. Receivers decode with the same validation as a file import and discard on any failure.

session.description: Session subset. For transport 'fragment', operator must be absent (enforced by the conditional below).

payload.description: The target product's own import shape: { schema: 'system-by-dave.<target>.v1', meta, items } (the sbd.handoff.v1 contract in js/sbd-handoff.js). For transport 'fragment' it must be small and free of personal data.

storageRecord.description: Where context and handoffs rest. Keys: '<client>.<product>.v<N>' for product state, '<client>.context.v1' for context, '<client>.handoff.<targetProduct>.v1' for a staged handoff. Staged handoffs expire after expiresAt and are always consumed on read. A migration from a legacy key is copy-then-verify-then-remove, never destructive first.
